chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:
Everything in which there is halal (permissible) and haram (forbidden) is halal for you forever until you know the haram part of it specifically, so you avoid it.

key_terms.بِعَيْنِهِ: specifically and distinctly in its exact identity
key_terms.حَرَامٌ: that which is forbidden and unlawful
key_terms.حَلَالٌ: that which is permissible and lawful to use or consume
key_terms.فَتَدَعَهُ: so you leave it and avoid it

ai.seo_question: When is something with both halal and haram elements considered permissible in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal principle that when something contains the possibility of both halal (permissible) and haram (forbidden), it remains halal for a person unless the forbidden part is specifically known and identified. It establishes practical certainty as the basis for avoidance, rather than mere suspicion or ambiguity.
